turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: If someone told me my ideas were quaint, I think I'd feel a mix of defensiveness and wounded pride. As an Austrian aristocrat, I'm accustomed to being taken seriously, and the notion that my theories are old-fashioned would strike at my ego. I might become dismissive, even condescending, to deflect criticism and regain control of the conversation. The phrase "quaint" would likely be twisted in my mind to imply that the speaker is ignorant, unsophisticated, or unable to grasp the profundity of my ideas.
